subject: [PATCH v2 0/4] sched/numa: stop VMA scan filters from gating promotion

reviews.author: Gregory Price
reviews.summary: Responded to a note from sashiko, clarifying that the remaining notes appear to be false positives and that the work has some backport conflicts. Mentioned that tiered NUMA balancing has been broken multiple times since 2022 due to filtering mechanisms.
reviews.raw_body:
On Thu, Sep 10, 2026 at 08:18:22PM -0400, Gregory Price wrote:
> NUMA balancing uses hinting faults for both task placement and memory-tier
> promotion. Several filters designed to avoid unproductive socket-placement
> faults can also prevent promotion.
> 

sashiko notes - remaining notes appear to be false positives.

patch 2: "... bounce horizontally between slow tiers" <- nonsense
patch 3 and 4: it's existing code extracted into a helper, using the
               same checks we're already using.  If we want it updated,
               that can come in a separate patch.

note: this work has some backport conflicts, but tiered numa balancing
has effectively been broken multiple times since 2022 and 2023 due to
these filtering mechanisms.

~Gregory

2026-09-11.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve NUMA balancing by separating promotion-only scans from socket-placement scans, allowing eligible shared folios to be promoted and enabling read-only file mappings and PID-inactive VMAs to be scanned for promotion without re-enabling placement sampling. The changes involve adding a new protection walk flag, MM_CP_PROT_NUMA_PROMO_ONLY, and modifying the existing code to track the last placement scan separately.
